claims.text: A post-processing aging treatment can introduce controlled coherent nanoprecipitates into an additively manufactured refractory high-entropy alloy.
The induced coherent nanoprecipitates will be uniformly dispersed throughout the alloy matrix.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation will improve the helium-irradiation tolerance of the RHEA.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as efficient sinks for radiation-induced point defects.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as efficient sinks for radiation-induced dislocation loops.
Enhanced annihilation of radiation-induced defects will reduce helium-bubble nucleation and growth.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could otherwise initiate premature cracks.
SCCP can provide a refractory high-entropy alloy with high strength and tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
SCCP-treated refractory high-entropy alloys can retain high strength at elevated temperature.
The SCCP-treated alloy will maintain strength and ductility relative to the untreated baseline after helium irradiation.
The treated alloy will exhibit lower helium-bubble density than the untreated alloy under identical irradiation conditions.
The treated alloy will exhibit smaller helium bubbles than the untreated alloy under identical irradiation conditions.
Compositionally complex refractory alloys can be fabricated using additive-manufacturing routes.
Increasing compositional complexity and entropy may increase helium-irradiation tolerance in additively manufactured RHEAs.
A homogeneous microstructure free of elemental segregation may improve helium-irradiation performance.
Combining additive manufacturing with an SCCP aging treatment is an engineering-practical manufacturing route for plasma-facing RHEA components.
The beneficial effect should hold only within a precipitate-size and dispersion window that preserves matrix connectivity.
The effectiveness of SCCP under irradiation may vary with alloy composition and heat-treatment parameters.
